title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: usage reports for Copilot Search, connectors and agents in US Government clouds
summary: Hold: the page asserts automatic availability and included licensing without published evidence, and its report-privacy API example lacks a required Boolean value. The roadmap details match, but report navigation is presented as an access control and the absence of access-management automation is incorrect.

claims.claim: Copilot reports are reached in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
To view reports, go to Reports > Usage.
Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage:

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for administering access to Copilot usage reports.
claims.quote:
Create a role assignment for the directory provider:
POST /roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Separate report navigation from access administration. Microsoft Entra reporting roles can be assigned through POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments with principalId, roleDefinitionId and directoryScopeId. Replace this absence with that documented general role-assignment mechanism and its reference URL, or remove the misleading access-control row and describe navigation in prose.

claims.claim: Report-name concealment is configured at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
Select Org Settings.
On the Services tab, select Reports.
In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { displayConcealedNames } is the documented request for changing report-name concealment.
claims.fix: Use a valid JSON Boolean body: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { "displayConcealedNames": true }. Explain that true conceals names and false reveals them. Link to https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/adminreportsettings-update?view=graph-rest-beta, which documents the method and path, and disclose that beta APIs can change and are unsupported in production applications. The endpoint exists and its beta deployment table includes US Government L4 and L5; the pre-check's missing-string result alone is not proof of a nonexistent API.

claims.claim: Report-name concealment is a tenant-level report setting.
claims.quote: Represents the tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports.
